messages:
maria: Quick sync — follow-up to the kernel-selection + attention-opt RFC. We need decisions on the per-model policy surface, how to represent compatibility, and an emergency fallback strategy. Keeping this thread for short proposals and action items.

ajay: TL;DR: prefer a policy-first approach. Model metadata tags + a lightweight policy engine that evaluates per-request constraints (latency SLO, cost ceiling, accuracy tier) and picks the kernel.

dylan: Agreed. Question: how do we encode compatibility constraints without exploding config size? my idea: attach a small 'compatibility' blob to model versions that lists supported kernels + soft constraints. Example YAML:```
compatibility:
  model_tags: ["gpt-like","dense-attn"]
  kernels:
    - name: opt-fast
      max_seq: 1024
      quant: q4_0
      fallback: opt-safe
    - name: opt-safe
      max_seq: 4096
      quant: q8_0
```
This stays with the model metadata and runtime merges it with policy rules.

tess: Concern: per-model enablement = flag proliferation. We should avoid boolean flags per model/version. Instead expose a policy rule language and a single feature gate for the policy engine version. Models opt-in by having the compatibility blob present.

infra-bot: infra-bot: feature-flag "kernel_policy_v1" toggled ON in staging (by @maria).

simone: For safe roll-forward we should do a spiral canary: enable for 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated health gates (p95 latency, error-rate, cost delta). If any gate trips, auto-fallback to a compatible kernel.

ajay: Implementation sketch for a spiral toggle:```
# example CLI (infra-cli)
infra-cli feature set kernel_policy_v1 --percent=5 --match-models="^my-company-.*-prod$"
# to advance
infra-cli feature set kernel_policy_v1 --percent=20
```
Plus a CI job that promotes percentages on green metrics.

dylan: On the runtime side we need a compact fallback chain evaluation. We should stop selecting a kernel that reports a recoverable runtime code and immediately attempt next compatible kernel. e.g., on `KV_CACHE_MISS` or `KERNEL_OOM` try fallback. Minimal policy: max retries 2, backoff 200ms.

maria: Telemetry: let's capture kernel_selected, fallback_attempts, fallback_reason, request_seq_len, p95_token_latency, and cost_estimate. Dashboards should show per-model and per-kernel trends and a regression alert if quality metrics (our eval harness) degrade after changes.

tess: Also capture compile-time compatibility mismatches (when model's compiled ops aren't supported by candidate kernel) as an event so we can triage failed enrollments.

ajay: Small note on the policy schema — include a `priority` field to prefer low-cost kernels when within latency SLOs. Example: `priority: cost_aware` or `priority: low_latency`.

simone: SLOs we should gate on during spiral: p95 latency (< X ms, per model class), 5xx rate (< 0.5%), and per-token cost delta (< +25% vs baseline).

dylan: I'll prototype a compatibility shim that sits between selector -> kernel and emits structured logs. If selector returns kernel K with `compat=false`, shim will pick next entry in list. If none found, it returns an HTTP 503 with a clear error and kicks a pager.

maria: Action items: (1) ajay: draft Policy Schema V1 (fields + examples) by EOD Wednesday; (2) dylan: prototype compatibility shim + fallback chain by next Tue; (3) tess: telemetry dashboard spec + alert thresholds by Fri; (4) simone: spiral promotion automation doc and gate checks by next Wed. I'll open a short PR to the RFC repo linking this thread.

ajay: sgtm. I'll include a tiny JSON schema and a few real-world rules in the PR.

dylan: on it. I'll also add a small unit test that simulates kernel OOM -> fallback picks opt-safe.

tess: I'll stub dashboards and share screenshots in #eng-observability when ready.

maria: One behavioral decision to confirm: default behavior for models without a compatibility blob — do we: (A) keep existing selection logic (current heuristics), or (B) treat as 'no-policy' and force a conservative kernel? leaning (A) for compatibility, but we should document recommended onboarding. Thoughts?

simone: Lean (A) too. Gradual onboarding reduces churn. But enforce a migration audit: flag models without blob and recency of use so we can prioritize high-traffic models.

ajay: +1 (A). We'll surface a migration dashboard listing top models by traffic without compatibility blobs.

maria: Perfect. If nobody objects I'll lock these action items and assign owners. Thanks all — short sync but enough to start work. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: infra-bot: Created task tracker issue #4278 for "Policy Schema V1" assigned to ajay.
